articles.title: The JWST May Have Found Where Heavy Black Hole Seeds Formed
articles.description: Astrophysicists think that black holes grow through a hierarchical merger framework. But the elusive Intermediate Mass Black Holes are the missing link between stellar mass black holes, and the gargantuan supermassive black holes like the one at the center of the Milky Way. The JWST may have found the ancient sources of IMBH heavy seeds: young massive clusters in the high-redshift Universe.
articles.summary: JWST observations may have revealed where intermediate-mass black hole seeds form, solving a major astrophysical puzzle about supermassive black hole origins.

articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 is about to reach a historic one-light-day milestone
articles.description: NASA’s Voyager 1 is approaching an extraordinary milestone nearly 50 years after its launch, even as engineers battle dwindling power and mysterious technical problems. A clever energy-saving maneuver has extended the spacecraft’s scientific mission, while an unexplained 48-hour communications blackout recently gave NASA a scare. On November 18, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of one light-day from Earth, making even the simplest round-trip communication take 48 hours.
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 is approaching the remarkable milestone of traveling one light-day from Earth after nearly 50 years in space. This enduring probe continues transmitting groundbreaking data from the interstellar medium.

articles.title: All 5 genetic “letters” of DNA and RNA discovered in a 4.5-billion-year-old asteroid
articles.description: Scientists have discovered all five essential nucleobases used in DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, revealing that key ingredients for life existed in space billions of years ago. The remarkable finding adds to growing evidence from other asteroids and meteorites that these molecules were widespread throughout the early Solar System.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered all five nucleobases essential for DNA and RNA in pristine samples from asteroid Ryugu, confirming that life's chemical building blocks exist throughout the cosmos. This extraordinary finding supports theories about the universal distribution of biological precursors.

articles.title: Two Different Kinds of Gamma-Ray Bursts Erupted 4 Minutes Apart. Astronomers Have Never Seen This Before.
articles.description: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are among the most energetic cosmic events since the Big Bang, releasing the most energetic type of radiation, gamma rays – the stuff that turned unassuming Bruce Banner into the rampaging Hulk, but on an astronomical, potentially plan…
articles.summary: Astronomers have observed two different types of gamma-ray bursts erupting just 4 minutes apart—an unprecedented cosmic event never before documented. This rare occurrence provides extraordinary insights into some of the universe's most energetic phenomena.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory Spots Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto—the Biggest in 20 Years
articles.description: The distant, icy celestial body could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.
articles.summary: Rubin Observatory has identified a possible dwarf planet beyond Pluto—the largest such discovery in 20 years—that could become our solar system's sixth dwarf planet. This remarkable find demonstrates the power of modern observatories to reveal hidden worlds.

articles.title: Happy 65 Years: NASA’s Johnson Space Center Then and Now
articles.description: Sixty-five years ago, a bold vision took root in Houston: a NASA center dedicated to human spaceflight. Since its founding, NASA’s Johnson Space Center has helped lead the nation’s human spaceflight program, supporting missions from Project Mercury through Artemis. Today, Johnson serves as NASA’s Center of Excellence for Human Spaceflight, and its workforce is helping […]
articles.summary: NASA's Johnson Space Center celebrates 65 years of pioneering human spaceflight, from its founding in Houston to becoming the heart of astronaut training and mission control. This milestone reflects decades of achievement in advancing space exploration.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have revealed the ghostly Cat's Head Nebula, a star-forming region of remarkable beauty and scientific interest. These observations showcase the combined power of humanity's greatest observatories.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully lifted off toward Mars's moon Phobos, marking an ambitious Japanese-led endeavor to study the Red Planet's intriguing satellite. This mission will provide unprecedented data about Phobos and Mars system dynamics.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates eight years in space on its anniversary, continuing its groundbreaking journey to study Mercury with unprecedented scientific instruments. This ESA/JAXA mission represents one of humanity's most sophisticated planetary exploration efforts.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope has discovered a previously unknown comet during its mission to map the universe. This discovery demonstrates how modern observatories continue to reveal new objects in our solar system.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is scheduled to launch on October 19 from Japan's Tanegashima Space Center aboard an H3 rocket. This bold mission will explore Mars's enigmatic moon Phobos and advance our understanding of the Mars system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The Solar Orbiter spacecraft has discovered and tracked mysterious S-shaped magnetic structures called switchbacks in the solar wind, advancing our understanding of solar physics.

articles.title: A Virtual Lifeless Earth Will Help Scientists Find Life on Exoplanets
articles.description: Researchers have created a model lifeless Earth that couples the atmosphere with interior planetary processes. The model can reproduce Earth's modern habitable state without including life, showing that a planet that appears habitable isn't necessarily inhabited. The tool will be useful when and if the Habitable Worlds Observatory is launched, by helping identify false positives.
articles.summary: Scientists have created a virtual lifeless Earth model that integrates atmospheric and planetary interior processes to help identify biosignatures on exoplanets.

articles.title: The Vera Rubin Has Found Two More of the Milky Way's Dim Satellites
articles.description: The Vera Rubin Observatory has detected two more of the Milky Ways' dim, hard to see satellites. One is an ultra-faint dwarf galaxy, and one is a globular cluster. Each one is a missing piece of the puzzle in the Milky Way's merger history. By finding more of these satellites, our understanding of galaxy growth, and the role dark matter plays in it, will improve.
articles.summary: The Vera Rubin Observatory has identified two additional ultra-faint satellite galaxies orbiting the Milky Way, deepening our understanding of galactic structure.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Solved a Puzzling Contradiction in the Ryugu Sample
articles.description: Samples from the asteroid Ryugu, and from carbonaceous chondrites that have crashed on Earth, present an apparent contradiction. Their fine-grained matrices have widely varied compositions of their clay-like minerals. That suggests that there were widely different aqueous environments in the same parent bodies, which seems unlikely. But new research may have solved that contradiction.
articles.summary: Scientists have resolved contradictions between samples from asteroid Ryugu and Earth meteorites, advancing understanding of solar system composition and asteroid science.

articles.title: Leviathan's sprawling stars challenge idea that dusty giants become compact galaxies
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have confirmed a massive, dust-rich galaxy called Leviathan in the early universe. Seen when the universe was roughly 1.5 billion years old, the galaxy has its stars spread out rather than in a concentrated fashion. A paper, describing its strange stellar distribution, was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 19.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST observations of the massive galaxy Leviathan challenge existing models of how dusty galaxies evolve into compact forms. This discovery expands our understanding of galactic transformation in the early universe.

articles.title: NASA is racing against time to save the Hubble Space Telescope
articles.description: NASA is exploring a daring plan to save the legendary Hubble Space Telescope from its eventual fiery plunge into Earth's atmosphere. After more than 35 years of groundbreaking discoveries, Hubble is slowly losing altitude, and without intervention, it could fall back to Earth as early as 2033 or 2034. To keep the iconic observatory operating, NASA is asking private space companies to propose innovative ways to boost Hubble into a higher orbit, upgrade its capabilities, or safely dispose of it when its mission finally ends.
articles.summary: NASA is developing innovative plans to extend the operational life of the legendary Hubble Space Telescope and prevent its atmospheric reentry. This mission represents humanity's commitment to preserving one of our greatest scientific instruments.

articles.title: NASA smashed into an asteroid. Now Hera is closing in to see what happened
articles.description: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has captured its first clear view of two asteroids involved in NASA’s historic 2022 experiment to redirect a potentially dangerous space rock. Now approaching the pair, Hera will investigate the mysterious aftermath of the collision and uncover why the asteroid shifted far more than scientists predicted.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft has obtained unprecedented close-up images of the asteroids from NASA's historic DART kinetic impact experiment. This collaborative mission provides crucial data on the effectiveness of planetary defense techniques.

articles.title: NASA’s Perseverance Mars rover breaks historic record after traveling 28 miles
articles.description: NASA’s Perseverance rover has set a historic record by traveling 28.10 miles across Mars, farther than any vehicle has ever driven on another world. Armed with groundbreaking autonomous navigation technology and increasingly advanced driving capabilities, the rover is pushing the boundaries of robotic exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover has broken its own distance record by traveling 28.10 miles across the Martian surface. This achievement demonstrates the remarkable longevity and capability of advanced rover technology in exploring the Red Planet.

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
articles.description: Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive “ghost particles” could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universe’s greatest mysteries.
articles.summary: The IceCube detector has captured neutrinos with energies billions of times greater than solar neutrinos, revealing new insights into cosmic particle acceleration. These ghost particles offer a unique window into the universe's most violent phenomena.

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
articles.description: Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered a theoretical loophole that could permit black holes to split under specific exotic conditions. This groundbreaking theoretical work expands our understanding of black hole physics and spacetime dynamics.

articles.title: Ancient star collisions could explain mysterious Little Red Dots and 'impossible' black holes
articles.description: Collisions between stars in the early universe were common, and this could explain the growth of supermassive black holes and the existence of strange Little Red Dots seen by the James Webb Space Telescope.
articles.summary: Research suggests that stellar collisions in the early universe may explain the formation of mysterious 'Little Red Dots' and unexpected supermassive black holes. This model provides elegant solutions to long-standing cosmological puzzles.

articles.title: Dimorphos in sight: Europe's Hera probe gets its 1st look at battered space rock (photo)
articles.description: Europe's Hera planetary defense spacecraft is closing in on the binary asteroid system targeted by NASA's DART deflection test, and can now tell the two rocky bodies apart.
articles.summary: Europe's Hera spacecraft completes its first observations of the asteroid binary system previously targeted by NASA's DART planetary defense mission. This follow-up investigation will assess the effectiveness of humanity's first kinetic impact experiment on an asteroid.

articles.title: Nanohertz Gravitational-Wave Constraints on Supermassive Binary Black Holes at Cosmic Dawn
articles.description: Author(s): Yiqin Chen, Shi-Yi Zhao, Xingjiang Zhu, N. D. Ramesh Bhat, Jacob Cardinal Tremblay, Małgorzata Curyło, Valentina Di Marco, George Hobbs, Wenhua Ling, Rami F. Mandow, Richard N. Manchester, Saurav Mishra, Daniel J. Reardon, Sparrow Roch, Christopher…
articles.summary: Researchers have used gravitational wave data to constrain the population of supermassive binary black holes at cosmic dawn, revealing insights into black hole formation in the early universe. This work advances our understanding of how the most massive objects in the cosmos assembled.

articles.title: Researchers May Have Discovered the 6th Dwarf Planet
articles.description: The other five are Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.
articles.summary: Astronomers may have identified a sixth dwarf planet in our solar system, joining Pluto, Ceres, Eris, Haumea, and Makemake. This discovery continues to expand our understanding of the icy bodies populating the outer solar system.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered a large icy object beyond Pluto designated 2026 ED138 that could qualify as the solar system's sixth dwarf planet. This find represents a major discovery in our understanding of the outer solar system.

articles.title: La Chine dévoile sa feuille de route lunaire : trois lancements non habités, puis des astronautes sur la Lune avant 2030
articles.description: La Chine devrait envoyer des astronautes sur la Lune d'ici trois ans. Ce calendrier, dévoilé le 31 octobre lors d'une conférence à Pékin, montre la maturité du programme lunaire chinois. En France, on suit régulièrement les avancées et les déconvenues du prog…
articles.summary: China has unveiled an ambitious lunar roadmap featuring three uncrewed missions followed by human landings before 2030. This bold initiative represents a major milestone in humanity's return to the Moon.

articles.title: APOD: 2026 November 4 – The Not-So-Hidden Galaxy, IC 342
articles.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 4 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss   APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Not-So-Hidden […]
articles.summary: The Astronomy Picture of the Day features IC 342, a nearby spiral galaxy that reveals stunning details when observed carefully. This hidden gem showcases the beauty of galactic structure visible to patient astronomers.

articles.title: Before the Dawn in America’s Heartland
articles.description: With hardly a cloud in sight, astronauts had a sweeping view of nighttime lights in the U.S. Midwest.
articles.summary: Astronauts aboard the International Space Station captured breathtaking views of nighttime city lights across America's Midwest. The unique perspective from orbit reveals the human presence and infrastructure across the heartland.

articles.title: NASA Astronaut, STEM Creator Connect with Students for STEM Day
articles.description: Students across the country will have the opportunity to connect directly with the International Space Station during a live, interactive in-flight call with NASA astronaut Anil Menon and Mark Rober STEM content creator and founder of ClassCrunchLabs Foundation. The event, hosted by NASA’s Office of STEM Engagement, celebrates National STEM Day by bringing real‑world science, […]
articles.summary: NASA astronauts and STEM educators connected with students worldwide during a special outreach event from the International Space Station. The initiative inspires the next generation of space explorers and scientists.
